correctness.summary: For s=lambda+mu<1, a paired alternating Riemann-sum lemma gives the endpoint coefficient asymptotic -(1/2)n^(1-s) along even n. The shift correction is lower order, and the same lemma applied to u^(-s)sin(yu) gives n^s S_n(pi-y/n)->-(1/2)sin y. This forces negative values below the threshold. The converse direction s>=1 is the published Sangal-Swaminathan positivity theorem.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The Sangal-Swaminathan source and its Cesaro application state the sufficient range lambda+mu>=1 but no sharp converse or boundary-layer profile was found. Searches by exact coefficients, authors, Vietoris/Belov terminology, sharpness/necessity, endpoint derivatives, and asymptotic formulations found no prior classification. Kwong's accessible manuscript states the general endpoint obstruction for a different family, so the novelty claim is limited to this coefficient family and its quantitative asymptotics. A differently phrased regularly-varying-coefficient theorem remains a residual risk.

value.summary: The theorem makes the exponent condition in a published Vietoris-type family exact and supplies a universal mechanism for failure below threshold: a shift-independent endpoint slope and 1/n boundary-layer profile.

limitations: Cosine positivity alone is not classified for lambda+mu<1.
Lower-order shift-dependent endpoint asymptotics are not derived.
A differently phrased theorem for regularly varying coefficients could overlap the converse.
Independent audit has not been performed.
